Four separated single-DNA daughter chromosomes form two groups of two moving toward opposite poles. Each V-shaped carrier has one spindle connection at its leading vertex. No sister-joining bridge or intact nuclear envelope remains. The selected cell is elongated; no physical velocity is encoded. Every centrosome retains two separate perpendicular centriole carriers, simplified from narrow closed rods to 13 mm centreline strokes. Their 36 mm PCM circles are enlarged independently; this is a didactic layout with no physical organelle-scale claim.
